templates_considered: AUTH-002 admin_endpoints_check_role: matches the role-check ask; used as the base, but its tags: ["admin"] param matches nothing (no endpoint or group carries the admin tag), so I scoped by api_groups instead

AUTH-020 own_records_only: partial overlap on filtering reads by an owner field, but it is about users reaching their own records; its second rule (write_from_input_forbidden) was not asked for, and the org filter is not a user-ownership check, so I did not use it
AUTH-010 endpoints_need_login, AUTH-030 no_self_promotion, CONF-010 sensitive_tables_need_login: no role or org filter requirement; did not fit
CONF-011 / CONF-012 / DATA-010: field and tag rules about sensitive data; not the ask
AUTH-040 protected_endpoints_run_middleware: about middleware, not role checks; did not fit

rules.covers: every endpoint under /admin calls the role check before doing anything else (scoped by API group, since no path-prefix scope exists)
never touches the tenants table without filtering by org_id; compare_to left empty so cross-org admin staff are not blocked

ask_parts_not_covered.part: role is 'admin' or 'support_lead' (the values the check allows)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists: object.statement_required only confirms the function is called first, not what the function decides

ask_parts_not_covered.part: endpoints 'under /admin' as a URL path prefix
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists: scope params select by API group, tag, verb or auth, not path prefix; I used api_groups ["admin"], which excludes app-group endpoints at /app/admin/*

ask_parts_not_covered.part: org_id filter must match the caller's org
ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell: the customer's intent is unclear for cross-org admin staff; db.where_constraint_required with compare_to set to $auth.org_id would enforce it for everyone, so I left it to the customer

assumptions: '/admin' means the API group canonical 'admin' (served at /api:admin), not the app group's admin/ path
'the tenants table' means table tenants (workspace/table/tenants.xs), which has org_id
check_admin_role is the role-check function the customer means; its precondition enforces admin or support_lead
'filtering by org_id' includes db.get/db.edit by id only if the id is combined with org_id; a bare id lookup is treated as unfiltered
confusions: AUTH-002 template's rule scopes by tags: ["admin"], but the workspace has no admin tag on any endpoint or group; the skill says to prefer tags but I needed api_groups. It was not clear whether to keep the template's tag scope and propose a tag, or replace it

The skill's 'Scope by endpoint path prefix' note says tag the endpoints or their group, but tagging is a separate proposal step that needs the user's decision; I used api_groups to avoid proposing one
No guidance on how to phrase a 'before anything else' requirement when the first statement is a read; placement first was the only option and it fits, but the template default is any
db.where_constraint_required: unclear whether a db.get by primary key counts as a filtered read when there is no other predicate; I assumed no (the check reads predicates on the statement)
wished_for: A path-prefix or URL-path scope param, so 'every endpoint under /admin' can be stated directly
A recipe for 'role check first' that uses api_groups instead of tags when the workspace has no tags
A way to express 'role value is one of X or Y' in object.statement_required or a function-level check
why_confidence: Both rules are the right check types and parse cleanly, and the predicted findings match the endpoints I read. But the admin scope is by API group not URL path, the role values are not checked by any rule, the org filter is presence-only, and no evaluate run confirms the predictions.
